nesnd_prussian_coalition_reason: France and the Confederation of the Rhine keep the German states apart. If Prussia is to contest their influence, it must convince the other states that Berlin will put its army behind their common interests.\n\nAlliances and defensive pacts tie the states together, and it is the army and the arsenals that make the promises good. States still answering to France or a Rhenish overlord must win back their freedom in foreign affairs before they can join.
nesnd_austrian_italy_reason: French-backed republicans, the ruling dynasties and the Pope all want to decide Italy's future. Austria can prop up the independent states with defensive pacts, or send troops to stop them being swallowed.\n\nIntervention takes money, and allies. If Vienna accepts the unifiers' gains, its word will carry far less weight in Italy.
nesnd_europe_america.2.d: The old order under which France ruled the German states is ebbing away. Prussia has come out of the contest with more weight, and the military and diplomatic ties it formed along the way will go on pulling at the states' choices.
nesnd_europe_america.3.d: Austria has taken the defending side in the Italian dispute. The envoys' promises now have troops and money behind them, and Vienna's prestige is staked on how the dispute ends.
nesnd_europe_america.5.d: Austria's intervention has failed to save what it set out to save. Territorial demands, a change of allegiance or the end of the protected state have left the original promise hollow. Every Italian state will remember this failure.
nesnd_europe_america.6.d: The dispute is over, and Austria has nothing to show that it could call a victory. The protected state survives, but not one of the disagreements has been settled.
nesnd_europe_america.10.d: The United States has demanded [SCOPE.sState('nesnd_usa_disputed_state').GetName]. The federal envoys call it restoring a rightful border; for the residents, landowners and garrison, it is a hard fight over sovereignty.
nesnd_phi_finance.3.d: The central government has approved garrison funding of #v £8,000#! a week for one year, and reduced tribute has been written into the proposal. The garrison and the Luzon squadron keep their present deployment and need not join the court's main force.\n\nThe money has been won, but Luzon must still feed its own troops and ships. Once we sign, how this money is divided between soldiers' pay and the people's livelihood is our own affair.
nesnd_phi_finance.4.d: The central government has agreed to the proposed division of naval duties. Under this arrangement, the ships of the line belong to the court's main force, while the frigates and the Western Administration's garrison remain in Luzon. The centre bears the upkeep of the ocean-going warships, allowing the Pacification Commission to concentrate on the islands' garrison and coastal defence.\n\nThe transfer of ships, reduced tribute and exemption from service are all in the proposal, with #v £3,000#! a week in subsidies for the first year. Once the warships are handed over, they belong to central command; if Luzon still struggles, it may ask for more funds. All that remains is for the Commission to sign.
nesnd_phi_finance.10.d: After several rounds of talks, the two countries have revised the military funding treaty. The payments and duties agreed before now follow the new terms.\n\nThe Pacification Commission must rework its spending under the new treaty: when the money arrives, which duties belong to whom, and how much is left for soldiers' pay and the districts, it is all written there.
nesnd_phi_finance.11.d: Luzon asks the central government to share the annual cost of its garrison and naval defence. The Pacification Commission is willing to remit tribute as before. It argues, however, that troops and ships awaiting the court's summons should receive part of their support from the central treasury.\n\nThe proposal requests #v £8,700#! a week for one year. The court's ocean-going forces and Luzon's own livelihood both eat from the same bowl: the islands' revenue. Leave the whole burden on the districts, and they will have nothing left to rebuild production.
nesnd_phi_finance.12.d: The central government has approved a subsidy of #v £8,700#! a week for one year. Tribute is remitted as before, the Pacification Commission still maintains the fleet and garrison, and the court covers part of the cost from its treasury.\n\nThe payments await only Luzon's signature. The subsidy will ease the immediate strain; the islands' affairs remain the Commission's to manage.
nesnd_phi_finance.14.d: The central government has accepted the proposal to divide naval responsibilities. Under its terms, twenty ships of the line belong to central command, while frigates and garrison troops remain to defend the islands. The upkeep of the transferred warships falls to the centre.\n\nThe Pacification Commission will receive #v £3,700#! a week for one year; tribute and exemption from service follow their own terms. With the military duties divided, the money saved can go to Luzon's own livelihood. The agreement awaits only our signature.
nesnd_small_dispute_organised: The government has allowed local organisations to operate, and the movements can now openly win supporters.
nesnd_small_dispute_suppressed: The police are suppressing local organisations, and the movements cannot act in the open.
nesnd_small_dispute_ended_conclusion: The political situation or the country's circumstances have changed, and the old way of handling the matter has been dropped.
nesnd_journal_closures_italy_agenda_conc: Public works and political cooperation in Italy have come to a close for now.
nesnd_journal_closures_hus_agenda_conclu: The local works and civic affairs run by the former Dongzhou government have been wound up.
nesnd_journal_closures_usm_agenda_conclu: The South's planned deliberations on the constitution, education and industry have come to nothing.
nesnd_journal_closures_small_livelihood_: The country's status or territory has changed, and the work on local livelihoods has come to a halt.
nesnd_supply_preparations_reason: Wu shipping brings grain from the Southern Seas, distant timber and foreign goods into the Southern realm. Inland workshops, garrisons and academies already depend on those exchanges. Provincial powers differ, but production and livelihoods can scarcely stand apart from the common market. Closing a port or severing a trade route spreads losses far beyond it.\n\nWhile the Ming court and Hangzhou fight over the succession, [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] cannot let its government or army stand still for a single day. Offices need paper, garrisons need men and weapons, and academy students are leaving the lecture hall for political life. Trade with willing partners must go on, and our own workshops, schools and villages must ride out this turmoil.
nesnd_supply_status_stable: #p Supplies, employment and livelihoods are becoming stable.#! Hold steady for one more season, and this trade can last.\n$nesnd_supply_rules_link$
nesnd_supply.1.d: Envoys from [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_supply_requester').GetName] have brought a request from their merchants: keep a purchasing line open between our countries, share news of paper, timber and workshop supplies, so that merchants can still find a way to trade however the situation turns.\n\nSending someone to talk means officials to receive them and merchants to do the business. [ROOT.GetCountry.GetName] could at least hear what they want to buy.
nesnd_supply.1.b: We cannot even keep our own house in order. The merchants will have to wait.
nesnd_supply.2.d: [SCOPE.sCountry('nesnd_supply_requester').GetName] proposes a formal treaty granting reciprocal trade advantages. Merchants hope it will open new markets, and buyers want steadier trading relations.
nesnd_supply_hus_preparations_reason: Immigrants and merchant ships built the republic's coastal towns. War against Wu brought its states together; the northern alliance opened further markets. Work in the harbours, production in the mills and provincial revenue now depend upon these connections.\n\nNow news of the Southern succession has crossed the ocean. Merchants ask after their supplies, shipowners fret about the sea lanes, and the workers are still waiting for their weekly wages. Whether we stay in the common market or go our own way, the first thing is to keep our own production, and our own livelihoods, steady.
nesnd_hus_registration_reason: Citizenship has never carried the same weight for everyone in the $HUS$. The Han come first, then Manchu and Mongol residents, Indigenous Americans and Europeans in turn: one country, but treatment divided into ranks. Now the argument over widening citizenship has reached the government. The Manchu and Mongols claim equality through their old ties to the Han; Indigenous peoples demand that the republic recognise their share in this land and this country.\n\nThe government can raise only one of them to first-tier registration, with the new law taking effect after a year of registration. Those left in the old ranks will remember this choice.
nesnd_hus_registration_manchu_conclusion: Manchu and Mongol residents now share first-tier registration with the Han. Indigenous Americans remain in the third tier and Europeans in the fourth. The ranks still stand; the first rank has simply grown larger.
nesnd_hus_registration_native_conclusion: Indigenous Americans now share first-tier registration with the Han. Manchu and Mongol residents remain in the second tier and Europeans in the fourth. The Manchu and Mongols have been left behind in the old hierarchy.
nesnd_hus_register_manchu_desc: The Manchu and Mongols have deep ties to the Han. Raising them to the first rank is the easiest step towards a wider citizenship.
nesnd_hus_register_native_desc: This land was the Indigenous peoples' home first, and they deserve the same standing as the Han. The Manchu and Mongols left in the second tier will look for a life elsewhere.
nesnd_egypt_independence_reason: The agreement of 1825 recognised Egypt's independence from Ottoman rule, and six powers guaranteed it in return for the right to invest along the Nile. The court won a breathing space, but its workshops, schools and army came to lean on foreign money and expertise.\n\nAn investment partner brings machines, teachers and new industries. Yet the more the foreigners own, the less Egypt can decide for itself. This is how it must live for thirty years.
nesnd_egypt_investor_none_desc: Egypt will walk its own road.
nesnd_egypt.1.d: Thirty years have passed, and Egypt has kept its own government and its own foreign policy. Foreign merchants still trade along the Nile, and the powers have not given up their schemes here, but Egypt's affairs have never been theirs to decide.
nesnd_egypt.3.a: This burden is ours alone to bear.
nesnd_egypt.4.d: Graduates of the university are entering the workshops, and the toolmakers and new industries now have a steady workforce. In the building still to come, more and more of the engineers and workers will be Egyptians.
nesnd_qe1.3.a: Ten years, wasted just like that.
nesnd_qe1_unity_journal_reason: Trade routes, villages and military colonies drew people of many origins under the rule of the Chen emperors of Qin. The Western Regions Han-Qiang are a product of the empire's expansion, and the empire's soldiers and revenue come from them. In good years, people are glad to share a common identity; when conscription grows heavy and times turn hard, the old clan names, faiths and home villages are dug up again.
nesnd_qe1_uprising_journal_reason: Petitions no longer satisfy the associations of the frontier. They are gathering provisions, approaching old noble families and religious leaders, and challenging imperial tax collectors and recruiting officers in the name of local peoples. Ili still has time to win back their loyalty; wait any longer, and the scattered revolts will join into one.
nesnd_qe1_recovery_journal_reason: The Chen imperial house cannot forget the passes of Hexi and the fields of Guanzhong. Win back the roads to the east, rebuild the army and the administration, and Ili can set out from the ancestral lands to contend for China once more.
nesnd_qe1_recovery.1.d: Qin forces have retaken the roads through Hexi and Guanzhong. The ancestral lands are ours again; how should this victory be used? March east with the new armies, or first let the new offices, industries and common identity take root in every province?
